label: Person
name: Gaius Sallustius Crispus Passienus
summary:
Gaius Sallustius Passienus Crispus was a prominent figure in the Roman Empire during the first century.

He held the consulship twice, and was stepfather of the future emperor Nero.

Born around 20 CE, Crispus's early life remains shrouded in mystery.

As a seasoned military leader, he played a crucial role in the Roman campaigns against Germania during the reign of Emperor Claudius.

Crispus's tenure as consul (34-33 BCE and 22-21 BCE) was marked by notable achievements, including the construction of roads and public buildings across Rome.

The Roman Senate eventually stripped Crispus of his consulship in favor of his son-in-law, Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, after discovering an alleged affair with a Vestal Virgin.

Crispus's legacy extends to his impact on the early imperial Rome, particularly through his influence on the reign of Nero.

One notable anecdote tells of Crispus being instrumental in securing the Senate's approval for Nero's rise to power.

The passage of time has left little clear evidence of Crispus's personal life, but it is well-documented that he died at 47 CE.
